title: OrbOracle: a stake-weighted, time-decayed price oracle
summary: Create your own on-chain price feed. Token holders stake to submit prices; the program keeps a weighted average that fades old submissions, pays submitters, and lets stakers vote out bad actors.
what: OrbOracle lets anyone create a price oracle tied to a **weight token**. Holders lock that token in the oracle's vault; once their lock period ends, the tokens count as voting weight. Each `submit_value` replaces the submitter's previous contribution in a token-weighted average whose older weight decays with a configurable half-life, so the feed follows recent, well-staked submitters. Submitters can earn SOL from the oracle account's balance, and stakers can vote to blacklist an address that submits bad values.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js 15 app, static export; only the program ID (in the app's IDL and types) and the base path changed. Oracle pages are served at `/o/?oracle=<address>` for static hosting.

try_steps.do: Make a weight token with **0 decimals** (the app's Deposit field sends whole base units): `spl-token create-token --decimals 0 --url devnet`, then `spl-token create-account <MINT> --url devnet` and `spl-token mint <MINT> 1000 --url devnet`, using the same keypair as Phantom or transferring the tokens to your Phantom address.
try_steps.see: 1000 tokens of your own mint in your wallet. Copy the mint address.

try_steps.do: Open [the Create page](/dapps/orboracle-solana/create/) and connect with the wallet button in the top bar.
try_steps.see: The Create Oracle form; the submit button reads "Connect Wallet to Create Oracle" until you connect.

try_steps.do: Fill in a name and description, paste your mint as the weight token, keep Reward 1000 (1%), Half-life 3600, Quorum 2000 and Alpha 1, and set **both lock periods to 5** seconds. Press **Create Oracle** and approve.
try_steps.see: An `initialize` transaction; the toast says "Oracle deployed" and the page shows the new oracle account (a PDA of your wallet and the mint).
ran: Create Oracle form (5 s locks): `initialize`; the page showed the oracle PDA CmAjgQFF…

try_steps.do: Open your oracle from **Explorer** (top bar). Enter `50` under Deposit and press **Deposit Tokens**; approve.
try_steps.see: A `deposit_tokens` transaction: 50 tokens move into the oracle's vault, locked for the deposit lock period.

try_steps.do: Wait a few seconds, enter a price such as `123.45` and press **Submit Value**; approve.
try_steps.see: A `submit_value` transaction. AGGREGATED and LATEST SUBMISSION both show 123.45 (you are the only submitter, so the average is your value).
ran: Submit Value 123.45; the page read back AGGREGATED 123.45 and LATEST 123.45

try_steps.do: After the withdrawal lock, enter `10` under Withdraw Weight Tokens and press **Withdraw Tokens**.
try_steps.see: A `withdraw_tokens` transaction: 10 tokens come back from the vault, and your weight drops to 40.
try_steps.ran_note: Withdraw was run from the script (B withdrew 40, 3WkpLLWv…), not clicked.

try_steps.do: Optional, with a second wallet that also deposited: enter the first wallet's address as **Target Address** and vote blacklist.
try_steps.see: A `vote_blacklist` transaction. Once the target is blacklisted, its next Submit Value fails with `AccountBlacklisted`.
try_steps.ran_note: Voting was run from the script (B blacklisted A, 7NJHE8SK…), not clicked.

diagram:
creator ── initialize(params) ─▶ OracleState PDA ["oracle", authority, weight_mint]   (~8 KB: params, aggregate,
                              └─▶ oracle vault = ATA(owner = OracleState, weight_mint)       128-entry price history, 64 vote targets)
anyone  ── fund(lamports) ─────▶ SOL into OracleState (the reward pool)
holder  ── deposit_tokens(n) ──▶ tokens ─▶ vault;  UserState PDA ["user", oracle, holder]: locked += n
           (after deposit_locking_period: locked → unlocked = voting weight)
holder  ── submit_value(v) ────▶ aggregate = time-decayed, token-weighted average (replaces holder's previous v)
                                 reward lamports: OracleState ─▶ holder
holder  ── withdraw_tokens(n) ─▶ vault ─▶ holder (PDA signs with seeds), after withdrawal_locking_period
holder  ── vote_blacklist / vote_whitelist(target) ─▶ targets[] tally; blacklisted addresses can't submit or vote
accounts: Parameters, aggregated / latest value, aggregated weight, history, vote targets; its SOL balance funds rewards
All staked weight tokens; only the OracleState PDA can sign for it
Locked / unlocked tokens, timestamps, last submitted price and weight, the user's votes

instructions.name: `initialize`: create the oracle and its vault
steps: Validates the parameters: non-empty name of at most 64 bytes (`InvalidName`), description ≤ 256, `reward_bps <= 100_000` (`InvalidRewardRate`). Our test hit both errors.
The account is a PDA of `["oracle", authority, weight_mint]`, so one wallet can run one oracle per weight token; the app checks for an existing one before sending.
`associated_token::authority = oracle_state` creates the vault owned by the oracle PDA.
Space is fixed up front for 128 price records and 64 vote targets (`OracleState::SPACE`), so the account never needs to grow.

instructions.name: `fund` and `deposit_tokens`: SOL for rewards, tokens for weight
steps: `fund` is a System Program transfer of SOL into the oracle account (zero is rejected with `AmountMustBePositive`). The app has no Fund button; our script funded 0.05 SOL.
`deposit_tokens` creates your UserState on first use (`init_if_needed`), first unlocks anything whose lock has expired, then transfers your tokens into the vault and adds them to `locked_tokens`.
Every deposit resets `deposit_timestamp`, so new tokens wait the full `deposit_locking_period` before they count.

instructions.name: `submit_value`: update the aggregate and pay the submitter
steps: Refuses blacklisted addresses (`AccountBlacklisted`) and anyone with no unlocked tokens (`NoUnlockedTokens`; our submit right after depositing was rejected).
Decays the global aggregated weight by the time since the last submission, and your own previous weight by the time since **your** last submission.

Removes your previous contribution (`last_submitted_price × your decayed weight`) from the numerator and weight, then adds the new value × your current unlocked tokens. One wallet therefore never counts twice.
New aggregate = numerator / new total weight. Values are integers with 6 decimals: 150.000000 is stored as `150000000`.

Reward: `reward_pool = oracle lamports × reward_bps / 100000`, scaled by your share of the weight and by how long since you last submitted (an activity factor), then moved directly from the oracle account to you.
Appends `(time, aggregate, value)` to the 128-entry history, dropping the oldest when full.

instructions.name: `withdraw_tokens`: get your stake back
steps: Only unlocked tokens can leave (`InsufficientUnlockedTokens`; our test asked for 101 of 100), and only after `withdrawal_locking_period` since your last operation (`WithdrawalLocked`).
Your vote weights are updated to the new balance (`apply_new_weight_to_votes`) before the tokens move.
The vault is owned by the OracleState PDA, so the transfer is signed with `new_with_signer` and the seeds `["oracle", authority, weight_mint, bump]`.

instructions.name: `vote_blacklist` / `vote_whitelist`: stake-weighted moderation
steps: Your weight is your unlocked tokens. You can vote once per target and kind (`AlreadyVoted`), for up to 64 targets.
A target is blacklisted when blacklist votes > whitelist votes **and** total votes > `quorum`.

Look at the units: the program compares the vote total (raw token base units) with `quorum` as stored. The app labels Quorum as basis points (2000 = 20%) and sends the number unchanged, so on chain the threshold is 2000 base units, not 20% of the stake. In our script B's 100 tokens (100,000,000 base units with 6 decimals) easily passed it and blacklisted A.

innovation.title: an O(1) decaying weighted average without floating point
innovation.text: The aggregate is updated in constant time per submission: the program keeps only the running numerator's result (`aggregated_value`) and the total weight (`aggregated_weight`), decays the old weight by elapsed time, swaps out the submitter's own previous contribution and adds the new one. No loops over submitters, no history needed for the math.
more: Decay is `2^(-elapsed / half_life)` in 18-decimal fixed point (`WAD = 10^18`). Solana programs avoid floats, so `process_pow2_neg_int` (lines 526–591) is a table of 2^-k for k = 0…60, and fractional steps are linearly interpolated between two table entries.
Rewards use the opposite curve, `1 - decay` (the activity factor, lines 638–645): the longer since your last submission, the more your next one earns. Spamming submissions earns almost nothing.
The reward pool is computed from the oracle account's **whole** lamport balance, which includes its own rent deposit, not only what was funded.

frontend.title: Create: derive the oracle PDA and vault, refuse duplicates, send `initialize`
steps: The PDA uses the same seeds as the program; `getAssociatedTokenAddressSync(mint, oracleState, true)` (the `true` allows an off-curve PDA owner) gives the vault.
It checks that neither account exists yet, then sends all parameters as one `params` struct. Quorum goes in as typed (see the units note above).

frontend.title: Deposit: whole base units
steps: `new BN(depositAmount)` sends the number exactly as typed, without multiplying by the mint's decimals. That's why Try it uses a 0-decimal mint.
Before sending, the app makes sure your token account and the vault exist (`ensureAssociatedTokenAccount`).

frontend.title: Submit Value: decimal text to a 6-decimal integer
steps: `parsePriceInput` turns `123.45` into the integer `123450000` without floating point (string padding), and rejects more than 6 decimals.
`submitValue` only needs your wallet, the oracle and your UserState PDA.

frontend.title: Votes
steps: The same three accounts; the method is `voteBlacklist` or `voteWhitelist` depending on the button.

exercises.title: Recompute the aggregate
steps: From Proof: A staked 300 tokens and submitted 150; B staked 100 and submitted 160 shortly after.
Compute the token-weighted average by hand.
exercises.expect: (300 × 150 + 100 × 160) / 400 = 152.5. The chain stored `152500778` (152.500778): slightly above, because A's weight had decayed a little in the seconds between the two submissions.
exercises.hint: The aggregate is a weighted average; the weights are stake × a time-decay factor. Every input is in the recorded submissions.
exercises.approach: Reproduce the formula from the program (don't guess the decay), plug in the recorded prices, stakes and timestamps, and compare to the on-chain aggregate after the last submission. They should match within the program's rounding.

exercises.title: Find B's reward
steps: Open B's submit transaction `63bZjLdC…` on Explorer and look at the balance changes, or compare the oracle's lamports in our log before (95,603,160 after funding) and after (95,284,351).
exercises.expect: The oracle account paid out 318,809 lamports, all to B. A's first submission earned 0 because the total weight before it was 0.
exercises.hint: The reward is paid from a collected fee or a reward pot, proportional to stake (and maybe to accuracy). Follow the token balances in B's reward transaction.
exercises.approach: From the recorded reward signature, read B's token-account delta and the pot's delta. They should sum to zero (plus fees) and match the formula. If B was paid more or less, you've found a bug to write up.

exercises.title: Watch a lock release
steps: Create an oracle with a 60-second deposit lock, deposit, and press Submit Value immediately.
Try again after 60 seconds.
exercises.expect: First attempt fails with `NoUnlockedTokens`; the second succeeds, because `unlock_tokens_if_possible` moves locked to unlocked once the lock has passed.
exercises.hint: Stake is often locked for a number of slots or seconds after a submission, so a submitter can't dump immediately.
exercises.approach: Try withdrawing before the lock ends (should fail with the program's lock error) and after (should succeed, as in the recorded release). The Clock or a stored `unlock_slot` is the judge.

exercises.title: Make quorum a real percentage
steps: In `refresh_blacklist_status` (line 928), compare against `total_deposited_tokens × quorum / 10_000` instead of `quorum`.
`anchor build` and test: total stake 400, quorum 2000 (20%), one voter with 50 tokens votes blacklist.
exercises.expect: With the fix, 50 < 80 (20% of 400): not blacklisted. A 100-token voter then pushes the total above 80 and blacklists the target.
exercises.hint: Same class of bug as Votara: a '10%' quorum that is compared to a raw count of submitters.
exercises.approach: Read the quorum check. If it isn't `weighted_stake * 100 >= total_stake * percent`, change it so that it is, and show a low-turnout submission that used to update the aggregate and now doesn't.

exercises.title: Derive your UserState
steps: In Node: `PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('user'), oracle.toBuffer(), you.toBuffer()], new PublicKey('3xqEVjy3zVjVnyb4qBa5xoBAQ9x4JhHowcV6JPQWXXqx'))`.
exercises.expect: The account your deposit created; on Explorer its data starts (after the 8-byte discriminator) with the oracle address and then your wallet.
exercises.hint: `UserState` is a PDA from the user and the oracle (or the feed). The seeds are in the Accounts struct.
exercises.approach: `findProgramAddressSync` with those seeds and the program ID. It must equal the UserState account in your submission transaction.

not_covered: Create, deposit and submit were clicked through in the hosted app. Funding, withdraw, blacklist voting and the blacklisted-submitter rejection were run from the script. Whitelist votes and `update_user_vote_weights` were not exercised. The app has no Fund button, and the explorer list uses getProgramAccounts on the public RPC, so it can be slow.
objectives: Run a stake-weighted price oracle: submit a price, see the aggregate, and watch old submissions fade with time.
Recompute the aggregate from the recorded submissions, and find a submitter's reward.
See a lock release and a quorum that may not be a real percentage.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 SOL, plus the oracle's stake token if the app mints one.
[stakes.wtf](/lessons/stakes-main/) (staking, rewards) and [Votara](/lessons/votara/) (quorum). This is an oracle, not a market: the output is a number other programs could read.
